subject: Startups
title: LPs: The Money Behind the Money
description: A 60-second lesson on LPs: The Money Behind the Money.

hook.text: VCs invest other people's money—not their own. The real backers are called limited partners, or LPs.

buildup.text: LPs include pension funds, university endowments, sovereign wealth funds, and wealthy families.

discovery.text: Harvard's endowment, Yale's fund, and CalPERS all invest in VC. Your pension might fund the next unicorn.

twist.text: LPs lock up their money for 10+ years. They can't withdraw early, even if the fund is performing badly.

climax.text: The VC ecosystem runs on patient, institutional capital. Without LPs, there would be no venture capital.

punchline.text: Behind every VC check is a pension fund's patience.

quiz.question: Who are the limited partners (LPs) in venture capital?
options: Institutional investors who fund the VC firm
